sections.title: Cosmology and Particle Physics
objectives: Discuss the expansion of the universe.

misconceptions.claim: String theory is a confirmed theory of everything.
misconceptions.correction: It is a promising idea that is still being tested, and it is not part of the standard model.

summary: Cosmology is the study of the character and evolution of the universe.

The two most important features of the universe are the cosmological red shifts of its galaxies being proportional to distance and its cosmic microwave background (CMBR). Both support the notion that there was a gigantic explosion, known as the Big Bang that created the universe.

Galaxies farther away than our local group have, on an average, a recessional velocity given by v = H 0 d,where d is the distance to the galaxy and H0 is the Hubble constant, taken to have the average value H0=20 km/s⋅Mly.

sections.title: General Relativity and Quantum Gravity
objectives: Explain the effect of gravity on light.

misconceptions.claim: Gravity bends light because it pulls on the mass of the photons.
misconceptions.correction: Photons have no rest mass. Gravity bends light because mass and energy curve spacetime, and light follows the curved path. The effect is predicted by general relativity.

summary: Einstein’s theory of general relativity includes accelerated frames and, thus, encompasses special relativity and gravity. Created by use of careful thought experiments, it has been repeatedly verified by real experiments.
One direct result of this behavior of nature is the gravitational lensing of light by massive objects, such as galaxies, also seen in the microlensing of light by smaller bodies in our galaxy.
Another prediction is the existence of black holes, objects for which the escape velocity is greater than the speed of light and from which nothing can escape.

authored_exercises.answer: A region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape from inside its event horizon.
solution: A sufficiently massive star can collapse under its own gravity.
The collapse concentrates mass into a very small region.
The escape speed near it exceeds the speed of light, so it appears black.

authored_exercises.stem: Why is quantum gravity difficult to construct?
authored_exercises.answer: General relativity describes gravity as smooth curved spacetime, while quantum mechanics describes the other forces with discrete quanta, and the two frameworks resist a simple combination.
solution: General relativity is a classical theory of geometry.
Quantum field theory describes forces by exchanging quanta.
At very small scales the two descriptions conflict and require new physics.

sections.title: Superstrings
objectives: Explain the relationship between Superstring theory and the Big Bang.

misconceptions.claim: Superstring theory is obviously false because we only observe three spatial dimensions.
misconceptions.correction: The extra dimensions predicted by string theory would be compactified or otherwise hidden at everyday energies. Their absence from ordinary experience does not rule the theory out.

summary: Superstring theory holds that fundamental particles are one-dimensional vibrations analogous to those on strings and is an attempt at a theory of quantum gravity.
Discuss the expansion of the universe.
Explain the Big Bang.

authored_exercises.stem: What is a superstring in superstring theory?
authored_exercises.answer: A tiny one-dimensional vibrating string whose different vibration modes correspond to different particles.
solution: The theory replaces point particles with extended strings.
Different modes of vibration give different masses and charges.
The strings are far too small to see directly.

authored_exercises.stem: Why is superstring theory attractive as a theory of quantum gravity?
authored_exercises.answer: One of its vibration modes has the properties of a graviton, so it naturally includes gravity.
solution: The theory describes vibrations of strings.
One allowed mode matches a massless spin-2 particle.
That particle is the graviton, the quantum of gravity.

authored_exercises.stem: Why is superstring theory difficult to test directly?
authored_exercises.answer: Its extra dimensions and string scale are far beyond the energies currently accessible to experiments.
solution: The strings are expected to be incredibly small.
Probing them would need energies far above those of current accelerators.
Many versions of the theory also make different low-energy predictions.

sections.title: Dark Matter and Closure
objectives: Discuss the existence of dark matter.
Explain neutrino oscillations and their consequences.

misconceptions.claim: Dark matter has been seen directly.
misconceptions.correction: It has not. Its presence is inferred from the rotation of galaxies and from the lensing of light, not from a direct detection.

summary: Dark matter is non-luminous matter detected in and around galaxies and galactic clusters.
It may be 10 times the mass of the luminous matter in the universe, and its amount may determine whether the universe is open or closed (expands forever or eventually stops).
The determining factor is the critical density of the universe and the cosmological constant, a theoretical construct intimately related to the expansion and closure of the universe.

authored_exercises.answer: Matter that does not emit, absorb or reflect light, but whose gravity affects the motion of galaxies and galaxy clusters.
solution: Galaxies rotate faster than their visible mass can explain.
Gravitational lensing shows more mass than we can see.
That unseen mass is called dark matter.

authored_exercises.answer: The change of a neutrino from one flavour to another as it travels.
solution: Neutrinos come in electron, muon and tau flavours.
A neutrino produced with one flavour can be detected later with another.
The oscillations show that neutrinos have mass.

sections.title: Complexity and Chaos
objectives: Discuss chaotic behavior of different systems.

misconceptions.claim: Chaotic systems are random, so their future cannot be predicted even in principle.
misconceptions.correction: Chaotic systems obey deterministic laws. Their extreme sensitivity to initial conditions makes long-term prediction impractical, but not impossible in principle.

summary: Complexity is an emerging field, rooted primarily in physics, that considers complex adaptive systems and their evolution, including self-organization.
Complexity has applications in physics and many other disciplines, such as biological evolution.
Chaos is a field that studies systems whose properties depend extremely sensitively on some variables and whose evolution is impossible to predict.
sections.no_worked_example_reason: The source carries no worked example for this section and no solved exercise to promote, so the practice is left to the exercises themselves.

authored_exercises.answer: A system made of many interacting parts whose collective behaviour is not obvious from the parts alone.
solution: Complex systems have many components.
The interactions produce emergent behaviour.
Examples include weather, ecosystems and the brain.

authored_exercises.stem: What does it mean to say that a system is chaotic?
authored_exercises.answer: Its future behaviour is extremely sensitive to its initial conditions.
solution: Chaotic systems follow deterministic rules.
Tiny differences in the starting state grow rapidly.
Long-term prediction therefore becomes impractical.

authored_exercises.stem: Why can a deterministic chaotic system still be unpredictable in practice?
authored_exercises.answer: Because any tiny uncertainty in the initial state grows exponentially, so predictions diverge quickly.
solution: The laws may be deterministic.
Measurements always have limited precision.
Sensitive dependence amplifies the error until the prediction is useless.

sections.title: High-temperature Superconductors
objectives: Discuss the need for a high-Tc superconductor.

misconceptions.claim: A superconductor is simply a perfect conductor with zero resistance and nothing more.
misconceptions.correction: Superconductors also expel magnetic fields from their interior, the Meissner effect. That distinguishes them from a merely perfect conductor.

summary: High-temperature superconductors are materials that become superconducting at temperatures well above a few kelvin.
The critical temperature Tc is the temperature below which a material is superconducting.
Some high-temperature superconductors have verified Tc s above 125 K, and there are reports of Tc s as high as 250 K.

authored_exercises.answer: A material that conducts electricity with zero resistance below a critical temperature.
solution: Below the critical temperature the resistance drops abruptly to zero.
A current can then persist without a power source.
Superconductors also expel magnetic fields.

authored_exercises.stem: Why would a room-temperature superconductor be useful?
authored_exercises.answer: It would carry current without resistive losses without needing expensive cooling.
solution: Ordinary conductors waste energy as heat.
Superconductors carry current with no resistance.
A room-temperature material would make power transmission and strong magnets much cheaper.

authored_exercises.stem: A superconducting ring at 4.2 K carries a persistent current of 100 A. (a) Why does the current continue without a power supply? (b) What is the Meissner effect? (c) Explain why a small magnet can float above a superconducting disk. (d) Why are high-temperature superconductors desirable for practical applications?
authored_exercises.answer: (a) The ring has zero electrical resistance, so the current decays only on an astronomically long time scale. (b) A superconductor expels magnetic field from its interior. (c) The expelled field produces currents that mirror the magnet and repel it. (d) They can be cooled with liquid nitrogen instead of expensive liquid helium.
solution: In the superconducting state, electron pairs move without scattering, so the resistance is zero and a persistent current does not decay.
The Meissner effect is the expulsion of magnetic flux from the interior of a superconductor as it enters the superconducting state.
A magnet near a superconducting disk induces surface currents that repel it. If the repulsion balances the magnet's weight, the magnet floats.
High-temperature superconductors have critical temperatures above 77 K, the boiling point of liquid nitrogen, which is much cheaper and easier to handle than liquid helium.

sections.title: Some Questions We Know to Ask
objectives: Identify sample questions to be asked on the largest scales.
Identify sample questions to be asked on the intermediate scale.
Identify sample questions to be asked on the smallest scales.

misconceptions.claim: Physics has almost no open questions left at the frontier.
misconceptions.correction: Many fundamental questions remain, including the nature of dark matter and dark energy, quantum gravity, and the origin of the matter-antimatter asymmetry.

summary: On the largest scale, the questions which can be asked may be about dark matter, dark energy, black holes, quasars, and other aspects of the universe.
On the intermediate scale, we can query about gravity, phase transitions, nonlinear phenomena, high- Tc superconductors, and magnetic effects on materials.
On the smallest scale, questions may be about quarks and leptons, fundamental forces, stability of protons, and existence of monopoles.
sections.no_worked_example_reason: The source carries no worked example for this section and no solved exercise to promote, so the practice is left to the exercises themselves.

authored_exercises.stem: Name one open question about the smallest scales of physics.
authored_exercises.answer: Why the elementary particles have the masses they do, or whether gravity can be quantized.
solution: The standard model does not explain the pattern of particle masses.
Quantum gravity remains incomplete.
These are active areas of research.

authored_exercises.stem: The Hubble constant is about 70 km/s per Mpc. Find the recession speed of a galaxy 10 Mpc away.
solution: Hubble’s law is v = H₀d.
v = 700 km/s.

authored_exercises.stem: Why is the nature of dark energy one of the biggest open questions in physics?
authored_exercises.answer: It makes up most of the energy content of the universe, yet its physical origin is unknown and its measured value is far smaller than naive quantum predictions.
solution: Observations show the expansion of the universe is accelerating.
Dark energy is the name given to whatever drives it.
Its nature and the tiny size of the cosmological constant are unexplained.
